newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Asian airlines oppose British noise rules.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Asian airlines oppose British noise rules.

text.p: The Orient Airlines Association (OAA), which groups 17 airlines in Asia and Australasia, said on Friday it would take legal action against plans by the British Government to impose tighter noise limits at major airports.

OAA director-general Richard Stirland said the International Air Transport Association (IATA) was taking action against the new limits which would take effect soon at London Heathrow, Gatwick, and Stansted.
"IATA has put an application to the High Court in London for a judicial review of the Minister for Transport's decision," Stirland told Reuters.

"If the application is granted there won't be a decision to impose noise levels from January 1997," he said. Stirland was speaking after the end of the two-day OAA executive meeting on the Gold Coast, southeast of Brisbane.

OAA chairman and Qantas Airways Ltd managing director James Strong said at a news conference earlier on Friday that airlines would take against against the new limits, particularly at Heathrow which Qantas used.

The Australian Financial Review newspaper said in its Friday edition that a Boeing 747-400 would be unlikely to meet the new limits set for night operations in London and major airlines would face fines of 1,000 stg for each breach of the permissible level.
